warnings: Rows are simulated and are not observations about real students.
Behaviour distributions are assumptions for development and testing.
Synthetic performance must not be reported as real-world model evidence.
External validity against a real university population was not assessed.

limitations: The synthetic data is generated and its statistical relationships may reflect simulator design.
KU Leuven and OULAD use different institutions, curricula, LMS schemas, and outcome definitions.
A significant feature-distribution difference is expected to be common across institutions and is not alone a reason to discard the synthetic dataset.
The comparison does not establish external calibration, fairness, causal validity, or intervention effectiveness.

feature_mapping.activity_count: synthetic study sessions versus LMS activity records
feature_mapping.content_count: distinct synthetic topics versus LMS content items
feature_mapping.mean_daily_activity: activity count divided by active observed days
feature_mapping.session_count: synthetic study sessions versus LMS sessions

real_world_comparison.interpretation: The real-world comparison is a stress test of measurement compatibility and risk prevalence. It cannot validate synthetic sleep, wellbeing, screen-time, or Indian-university attributes because the real datasets do not contain those constructs.
references: KU Leuven Open Data, Private Learners, 2021 locked test cohort

first_term_vs_last_term_risk_rate_test.interpretation: descriptive cohort-rate comparison; not a causal effect estimate

risk_association_tests.interpretation: A feature-level association is evidence of dependence in the generated records, not evidence that the feature causes academic risk. Strong associations may reflect simulator rules.

statistical_methodology.interpretation: P-values test distributional or rate differences under the observed sample; they do not establish causality, fairness, population representativeness, or intervention effectiveness. Effect sizes and domain context must be read together.

student_disjoint_split_validation.interpretation: These tests check whether the student-disjoint test cohort is compositionally different from training for the selected planner variables. A non-significant result does not prove representativeness; it only indicates that this sample did not detect a shift.
